prompt: Roadmap III, Prompt 220, Part B gate (docs/activity-ages-gate): gyrochronology ages and flare energies in erg
committed: before any prototype of an age or an energy existed, on this branch; the prototype is on spike/activity-ages-gate and is never merged. Nothing below was computed before this file was committed.
rule: A threshold that proves unmeasurable fails the gate on that threshold; only Carl resets one. Verdicts are by the rule under verdict, not by judgement afterwards.

mamajek2008.citation: Mamajek & Hillenbrand 2008, ApJ 687, 1264, Section IV.2 and Table 10 (read 2026-10-30 from arXiv:0807.1686)
mamajek2008.form: P = a ((B-V)_0 - c)^b t^n, P in days, t in Myr; inverse log t = (1/n) [log P - log a - b log((B-V)_0 - c)]
mamajek2008.scatter: precision of +-0.05 dex (1 sigma, +-11 per cent) in log t for coeval field binaries; the absolute cluster age scale adds about 15 per cent
mamajek2008.calibration: I-sequence rotators of alpha Per, the Pleiades, M34 and the Hyades (no cluster older than about 625 Myr), and the Sun (26.09 d at 4566 Myr); fast C-sequence rotators were excluded; metallicity ignored
mamajek2008.statedLimits: the authors say they lacked cluster sequences or single stars with accurate ages above 625 Myr, so ages beyond it rest on the solar datum, and that the relation is poorly constrained for late-F and early-G stars older than the Hyades; the surrounding analysis is for 0.5 < (B-V)_0 < 0.9

barnes2007.form: P = a ((B-V)_0 - 0.4)^b t^n, t in Myr
barnes2007.scatter: representative age errors of about 15 per cent plus possible systematic errors; the author notes errors above about 11 per cent under his assumptions; no cluster star is bluer than B-V = 0.5, so the function is extrapolated for 0.4 to 0.5

domain.note: this contract's domain for printing a number, the intersection of the calibration and the statements above
domain.sequence: the slow (I) sequence: a period below the relation's value at 100 Myr for the colour is a fast-rotator or pre-main-sequence period and gets no number
domain.readingOnly: ages between 625 Myr and 4566 Myr (anchored by the Sun alone), colours outside 0.5 to 0.9, M dwarfs, binaries, and any period the relation does not reach

flareEnergy.source: Shibayama et al. 2013, ApJS 209, 5 (arXiv:1308.1480): the white-light flare is a blackbody of 10,000 K; a flare temperature of 9,000 K gives 66 per cent of that energy; a few tens of per cent error is stated; stellar radius and temperature uncertainties of the Kepler Input Catalog of +-0.2 dex and +-200 K enter
flareEnergy.contractRange: 9000 to 11000 K about the source's 10,000 K (the contract's choice, not a citation)
flareEnergy.bandpass: the TESS response of data-packs/radiation-bandpasses.json (photon-counting relative response)
flareEnergy.definition: E_band = ED x L_star,band with L_star,band = 4 pi R^2 integral(pi B_lambda(T_eff) r(lambda) d lambda) (energy-weighted response r over the star's blackbody); the correction C(T_f) = sigma T_f^4 / (pi integral B_lambda(T_f) r(lambda) d lambda) turns a flare's band energy into its bolometric energy for a blackbody flare of temperature T_f; E_bol = C(T_f) x E_band

legs.what: the age recovered from the period the relation gives for 50 (colour, age) points over the domain, both relations
the same inversion in an independent numpy implementation written from the equations above at 20 pinned points per relation

2000 seeded stars with (B-V)_0 uniform in 0.5 to 0.9 and log t uniform over 100 to 625 Myr, a period drawn from the Mamajek relation with log-normal scatter whose age-equivalent is 0.05 dex (sigma log P = n x 0.05), the age recovered with an interval of +-1.96 x 0.05 dex about it: the interval contains the true age at the stated rate (a test of the interval's construction, stated as such: the sample is drawn from the relation it tests)
1000 seeded cases outside the domain (colour 0.2 to 0.49 or 0.91 to 1.6; periods giving an age below 100 Myr or above 625 Myr; periods below the I-sequence at 100 Myr): no number is returned for any

the age from each relation for the same (colour, period) over colours {0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9} and Mamajek ages {100, 200, 300, 450, 625} Myr: the 95th percentile of |log t_Barnes - log t_Mamajek| over the 25 points (if two published calibrations of the same kind differ by more than twice the stated scatter, the scatter is not the interval)

EK Draconis, a young Sun-like star: the periods 2.6 d and 2.77 d (the literature values of the Prompt 220 Part A contract) and (B-V)_0 = 0.61 (one older source, the weakest input of the gate): the age from each relation lies in 30 to 125 Myr, the span of the published ages of the star (50 to 125 Myr; 30 to 50 Myr from model atmospheres; 27 +11 -8 Myr in 2021); an applicability check, not a calibration
the repository's blackbody band integral over the TESS response against an independent numpy integral at 7000 to 12000 K in 1000 K steps

the ratio of the largest to the smallest C(T_f) over 9000 to 11000 K: a bolometric energy is a range, and a range wider than a factor of 1.5 from the flare temperature alone is not a number a student should be handed in erg

verdict.A: G1 to G7b all pass: ages with the scatter as the interval within the domain, and flare energies in erg with the temperature range
verdict.B: G1, G2, G3 and G4 pass and at least one of G5, G6, G7a, G7b fails: the age as a reading step with the relation shown and no number, no energy in erg (the equivalent duration stays in seconds)
verdict.C: any of G1, G2, G3 or G4 fails: no ages and no energies; Part A stands
